source.title: Elucidating an Affective Pain Circuit that Creates a Threat Memory

confidence_rationale: Causal circuit paper: CGRP parabrachial neurons project to CeA and carry affective pain; silencing them blocks pain responses and threat-memory formation, stimulating them produces defensive responses and a threat memory, and CGRP-receptor CeA neurons are needed to establish the memory. Supports MECH-599's structure of a dedicated affective-harm teaching pathway into a store that creates a threat memory. Does not address cue specificity or the injury/threat consumer split.
failure_signatures: Optogenetic stimulation of the affective pain pathway alone, without tissue damage, was sufficient to create a threat memory; a threat store whose teaching depends on accumulated injury rather than an affective harm event would not reproduce this.
Silencing the pathway blocked both pain responses and memory formation, so in this circuit the acute nocifensive response and the teaching signal are not cleanly separable at the input stage.

mapping.source_claim_statement: CGRP-expressing parabrachial neurons project to the CeA and may transduce the affective-motivational aspect of pain; genetic silencing blocks pain responses and threat-memory formation, optogenetic stimulation produces defensive responses and a threat memory, and CeA neurons expressing CGRP receptors are critical for establishing the memory.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-599's claim that a dedicated teaching pathway writes into a threat store: an affective harm event (not tissue damage per se) is sufficient to create a threat memory. The affective-pain identity of the pathway lines up with SD-011's z_harm_a stream -- but as a TEACHER of the store, not as the variable consumers should read, which is exactly the MECH-599 consumer contract.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Mouse, footshock. Shows a pathway that creates threat memory, not that the resulting memory is cue-specific or held in a discrete store. The same silencing blocks acute pain responses, so the teaching/response separation MECH-599 draws is not demonstrated at the input.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; genetic silencing and optogenetic stimulation of CGRP PB neurons and CeA CGRPR neurons; fear conditioning

confidence_components.notes: Cell, causal gain- and loss-of-function. Mapping moderate: supports the teaching pathway, not cue specificity or the consumer contract.
